newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - MIM to upgrade copper refinery.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - MIM to upgrade copper refinery.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it would spend A$50 million to increase production capacity at its copper refinery in the Queensland coastal city of Townsville.
MIM said Townsville's refining capacity would be increased to 255,000 tonnes a year from 210,000, matching the output of MIM's Mount Isa copper smelter which was now being expanded.

"Over the next two years, we will install additional refining cells and modernise existing ones, acquire new overhead cranes and other materials handling equipment and upgrade key systems in the refining process," said Townsville refinery general manager Stephen O'Donnell.
Copper rod production would cease at the end of 1996, with the focus on copper cathode output. This change would reduce the number of staff by 60, with further cuts expected, MIM said.

"The refinery is 37 years old," O'Donnell said. "This major investment and restructuring are designed to achieve best practice in copper refining and to ensure that the Townsville refinery has a continuing and expanding role as a producer and exporter of high quality refined copper," he said.
MIM shares closed five cents higher at A$1.59 on Tuesday.
